title: Actors & nonisolated Members
hints: Actor methods are awaited from outside; a `nonisolated` member isn't.
`nonisolated var label` may only read the `let name`, never `books`.
jsBridge: Actor members are isolated (so callers must `await`), but `nonisolated` members that only touch immutable `let` state can be called synchronously. That's the escape hatch for things like `description` or IDs.

compass.q: In JS, reading an object's constant field never needs `await`. Why does Swift need `nonisolated` to allow it on actors?
Can a `nonisolated` method read a `var`? Why is `let name` fine?
`nonisolated let` vs `nonisolated func` vs making the whole type `Sendable`: which is the right tool?
Conforming an actor to `Hashable` or `CustomStringConvertible` needs `nonisolated`. Why?
